neighbours.label: ' was' / ' were' as the passive auxiliary when the text says when or by whom a building or artwork was made (was completed / built / painted); it promotes ' completed'
fire: The old lighthouse on the cape was finished in 1874.
Most of these frescoes were painted by his students.
The stone chapel was erected in 1902 by local farmers.
According to records, the dam was completed in 1936.
Both statues in the square were carved from local marble.
The city's first library was constructed with private funds.
Experts believe the altarpiece was commissioned around 1480.
The station's glass roof was installed after the war.
quiet: The old lighthouse on the cape still guides ships at night.
Most of these frescoes show scenes from village life.
The stone chapel stands at the edge of the farmers' fields.
According to records, the dam supplies water to three towns.
Both statues in the square face the old town hall.
The city's first library now houses a small cafe.
Experts believe the altarpiece shows the donor's family.
The station's glass roof leaks during heavy rain.

notes: Probe: 'was' before built/painted/completed 0.31-0.58, before 'empty'/'very crowded' 0.16-0.27, so the near misses drop 'was' altogether.
